plan.title: SHIFT: 52-week hockey development programme
goals: Stronger lower body, hips and single-leg control
More stable puck protection and contact readiness
Build useful capacity with comfortable, controlled movement

eventWindows.name: Tryouts, exact dates to be confirmed
Checking-league season, exact fixtures to be confirmed

assumptions: The current five skating evenings remain the default until the actual team schedule changes: Thursday light roller, Friday light ice, Saturday medium ice or game, Sunday light ice and Monday hard ice.
Ice and roller durations of 60 minutes are editable planning placeholders. They are not measured time on ice, completed logs or a prescription to change coached practice.
Gym sessions include warm-up, ramp-up sets, all planned work and recovery, equipment setup, transitions and cool-down within 60 minutes. Thursday optional activity is at most 20 minutes.
The first calendar week starts Monday 23 November 2026 but the first prescribed activity is Tuesday 24 November. No missed Monday workout is created.
No mandatory gym or hockey is prescribed during 5-19 December holiday. Sunday 20 December is a return/rest day; normal training resumes 21 December with reduced lifting intensity.
No baseline strength, sprint, jump, skill score, heart rate or completed session is fabricated. First loads are calibrated with RPE and recorded technique.
Routine one-hand handling, weighted-puck work and deliberate fatigue-handling are not activated by default. Any loaded wrist rehabilitation follows the treating clinician, not a generic calendar.
Two short easy-bike blocks sit inside Tuesday and Friday gym budgets. Additional Saturday intervals are optional replacement work and are omitted in test, deload and taper weeks.
Known June-July tryout timing is a window. A confirmed event date triggers a 5-7 day taper by reducing sets, not by increasing conditioning.
Main lifts remain specific to the recorded variant and equipment. Machine settings and dumbbell load conventions must not be mixed when comparing progress.

Requested equipment replaces existing slots: medicine-ball throws replace a Tuesday accessory, trap-bar jumps replace Friday pogos in eligible weeks, cable or multi-hip work replaces one hip accessory, and ab slings replace reverse crunches. These are not additional workouts.
A squat belt requires a compatible purpose-designed and rated belt-squat machine or attachment. Owning a belt does not confirm that a cable, dip-belt or improvised platform arrangement is suitable.

The chest-supported resisted-running machine and hydraulic/pneumatic squat machine are identified only by description. Their exact model, manufacturer-permitted movement and staff-demonstrated setup must be confirmed before use. No airborne repetitions are prescribed on the unidentified squat machine.

A machine resistance level or pressure is not kilograms. Record its actual display and unit without converting an arbitrary setting into kg or an estimated 1RM. Stationary resisted running is logged by work seconds, not invented metres.

Outdoor shooting requires a safe backstop, dry footing and daylight or adequate lighting. Indoor dry release and video practice train related movement or decisions but are not shots or an accuracy substitute.

calibrate.name: Find the first comfortable working load
calibrate.instruction: After ramp-up sets, select a load that allows every prescribed repetition with the stated RPE and consistent technique. Start at the lower end when uncertain. No baseline kg is assumed.
calibrate.noHistory: Leave target kg blank until a real calibration set is recorded. A previously painful exercise is not calibrated under load.

lower-main.name: Lower-body main lift
lower-main.success: For the next occurrence of this same exercise and variant, add 2.5 kg only after all planned working sets were completed at or above target repetitions, every recorded set RPE is at or below its target and no target exceeds RPE 8. Do not progress a partial session or a session with missing RPE.
lower-main.repeat: If repetitions or the RPE cap were missed, repeat the last working load next time. A skipped or incomplete session is not a failed attempt.
lower-main.repeatedMiss: After two consecutive completed occurrences with actual target misses, suggest a 5-10% load reset or a reduced-volume week. The user reviews the suggestion; it does not silently rewrite the plan.
lower-main.deload: Use approximately 85-90% of the last comfortable working load, or less to meet RPE 6. No progression is earned during deload or taper.
lower-main.rounding: Round down to available plates. If an increment is unavailable, retain the current load until the smaller step is possible.

upper-main.name: Upper-body main lift
upper-main.success: Add 1 kg in the exercise-specific logging convention only after all planned working sets hit target repetitions at or below the stated RPE, with a cap of 8, comfortable grip and no later symptom increase. For floor press this means 1 kg per dumbbell; row values follow the library convention.
upper-main.repeat: Retain the load if a target is missed, a set is incomplete, RPE is absent or the wrist response is uncertain.
upper-main.repeatedMiss: Two target misses on two completed occurrences trigger a review and a suggested 5-10% reset, not an automatic load increase.
upper-main.deload: Use roughly 85-90% of the last comfortable load and meet RPE 6. No increase during a deload or taper.
upper-main.rounding: Use the nearest available increment at or below 1 kg. If the available jump is larger, repeat the current load or add one repetition within the prescribed range first.

accessory.name: Accessory double progression
accessory.success: Build from the stated repetitions to the stated repRange upper end. Once every set reaches that upper end with RPE at or below 8 and comfortable technique, add 1 kg using that exercise load convention and return to the lower end.
accessory.repeat: Repeat load and repetitions if form, range, symptom response or RPE is not acceptable. A different machine requires a new baseline.
accessory.repeatedMiss: After two completed sessions with actual misses, suggest a 5-10% reduction or one fewer set.
accessory.equipmentStep: For selectorised machines, use the smallest available step only if it stays within the RPE cap; otherwise continue repetitions at the existing setting.

bodyweight.name: Bodyweight control before load
bodyweight.instruction: Complete the exact prescribed range or hold first. Add one controlled repetition per side, or five seconds per side, only within the listed maximum. Add external load or a longer lever only after two comfortable completions. Do not progress through pain.

speed.name: Quality governs speed and jumps
speed.instruction: Use the exact distances, landing counts and full rests. Repeat the current dose until landings and mechanics remain consistent. Stop after two clearly slower timed repetitions, a repeatable decline greater than approximately 3-5% using the same reliable timing method, or technique deterioration. This is a coaching quality rule, not an injury prediction threshold.
speed.progression: The dated plan changes one principal variable at a time. Never shorten recovery to turn a speed session into conditioning. Loaded jumps and medicine-ball throws use a light individually calibrated implement; no automatic kg increases. Stationary resisted-running work is timed separately from track sprint results.

conditioning.name: Maintain the stated effort and recovery
conditioning.instruction: Choose resistance or pace to meet the prescribed effort without wrist loading. Complete the stated work and recovery. When all rounds are consistent, follow the next dated dose; do not add unscheduled rounds.
conditioning.optionalIntervals: At most one extra interval session weekly, and only when it replaces rather than stacks onto meaningful hockey load. It is omitted during deload, testing, holiday and taper weeks.

skill.name: Accuracy and symptoms govern skill progression
skill.instruction: Record actual duration, touches, errors and eyes-up observation, or actual shots and hits by zone. Increase one variable only after two clean symptom-stable sessions: up to 5% more clean touches, one extra target difficulty, or the next planned shot block. Keep the current level when errors or wrist symptoms rise.
skill.locked: One-hand handling, weighted-puck work and handling under deliberate fatigue remain locked until specifically appropriate under clinician guidance. Dry rehearsals never become shot attempts or accuracy data.

mobility.name: Comfortable controlled movement
mobility.instruction: Use the stated repetitions or hold times without forcing end range. A pinching hip or painful wrist is a reason to reduce range or stop, not stretch harder.

readinessRules.status: Coaching heuristic, not a medical readiness test or injury predictor
readinessRules.inputScales: Sleep quality, energy and mood use 1-5. Soreness uses 0-10, where 10 is most sore. Sleep is entered in hours.
readinessRules.formula: round(100 * sum(available normalised score * weight) / sum(available weights)); sleep=clamp(sleepHours/8,0,1), weight30; energy=energy/5, weight20; soreness=1-soreness/10, weight20; sleepQuality=sleepQuality/5, weight15; mood=mood/5, weight15. Clamp every component to 0-1.
readinessRules.missingData: Use available observations with their weights renormalised and identify a partial check-in. With no observations show no score. Never invent missing sleep, soreness or mood values. Bodyweight does not enter this score.

bands.label: Usual plan if symptoms and warm-up are normal
bands.action: Follow planned targets; the score does not override pain, illness or clinician restrictions.

bands.label: Review warm-up and recent load
bands.action: Keep the usual load only if warm-up is normal. Omit optional intervals when recovery is uncertain.

bands.label: Reduce today or recover
bands.action: The lighter-session suggestion retains ceil(75% of working sets), with at least one set, an RPE cap of 7 and at least three repetitions in reserve. Offer easy movement or rest when that is more appropriate. No maximal testing or additional intervals when readiness is poor.

readinessRules.overrideTriggers: Fewer than six hours sleep, soreness at least seven out of ten or illness also prompts the lighter/recovery option. Worsening wrist or grip symptoms pauses added skills and painful grip work regardless of score.
readinessRules.symptomOverride: Sharp or worsening pain, swelling, neurological symptoms, altered movement or illness overrides the score. Stop and seek appropriate clinical assessment when indicated.
readinessRules.repeatedLow: Three low-readiness days, worsening symptoms or two completed target misses prompt a review of skating, sleep and total training before a 5-10% reset or reduced-volume week.
readinessRules.workloadChart: Display seven-day load and the mean of the preceding four complete weeks descriptively. Require four complete weeks. Do not present an acute:chronic ratio as a safe zone or an injury risk probability.

deloadRules.explanation: After holiday and return, every fourth loaded calendar week is reduced. Weeks 3-4 are holiday recovery. Baseline/retest weeks also reduce training because assessments replace work.
deloadRules.fixedIceLimit: Off-ice deload does not make unchanged team practice a whole-body deload. Discuss a lighter skate or omit optional ice if fatigue persists.

gameRules.saturdayGame: Replace Saturday practice with the actual game. Omit optional Saturday shooting/intervals. Friday becomes a 15-20 minute primer or rest; omit its loaded lower-body blocks if the game is important or recovery is poor. Sunday becomes recovery/mobility if sore.
gameRules.unexpectedGame: Move or skip the closest fatiguing lower-body or interval session. Do not make up omitted volume on another day.
gameRules.within48Hours: Avoid new exercises, high-volume eccentric work and extra intervals during the final 48 hours before an important game or tryout.

testRules.priority: Familiarised, recovered and repeatable conditions. Defer testing if the preceding hard skate leaves abnormal soreness or performance is not representative.
testRules.fastProgress: When a change exceeds ordinary repeat-test variation and technique remains consistent, continue the same successful progression. Do not skip phases or raise every training dose.
testRules.slowProgress: If a test stalls, first check timing protocol, fatigue, sleep, adherence and symptoms. If two comparable retests and training logs show stagnation, change one training variable and reassess.
testRules.noUniversalBands: Use protocol-matched reference cohorts only. Personal baselines are the default; no invented amateur or professional cutoffs.

timingConventions.estimate: Every row includes an estimated block duration. Tempo X uses a one-second planning allowance while actual concentric intent remains fast. Rests are minimum planned recoveries; busy equipment may require dropping a low-priority accessory, never rushing sprints.
timingConventions.lastSetRest: The final working-set rest is normally zero because subsequent setup/transition is budgeted separately. Testing recovery measurements are explicitly retained.
timingConventions.sides: Repetitions and hold seconds on a target with sides:2 are per side. Warm-up/cool-down seconds are total allocated seconds across both sides.
timingConventions.contacts: Count individual foot contacts: one two-foot landing counts as two contacts, and one unilateral landing counts as one contact. Low pogo and demanding bound contacts are reported separately. Doubling the count for a bilateral landing does not add a jump.
timingConventions.strengthLoad: Use exercise.loadConvention. Bodyweight is not added to volume load; a dumbbell floor press is recorded per dumbbell and its external volume multiplier is two.

phases.name: Preparation, holiday and return
phases.focus: Establish repeatable baselines, wrist-tolerated movement, and a gradual return after holiday.
phases.intensity: RPE 5-6; approximately 50-70% of a known comparable 1RM where available.

weeklyTemplate.Mon: Hard evening ice only; no gym. Record actual duration and session RPE.
weeklyTemplate.Tue: Brief medicine-ball ballistics in suitable loaded weeks, then upper strength and short easy bike. Optional controlled handling only if the wrist tolerates it.
weeklyTemplate.Wed: Fresh speed and landing work, then main lower-body strength with belt-squat options. Test batteries replace this session in test weeks.
weeklyTemplate.Thu: Light roller. One optional mobility and comfortable walking session, maximum 20 minutes.
weeklyTemplate.Fri: Short lower power, including calibrated trap-bar jumps in eligible weeks, controlled strength, one hip accessory and easy bike before light evening ice. Reduce to a primer when Saturday is a game.
weeklyTemplate.Sat: Medium ice or occasional game. One optional skills module OR a conditional conditioning replacement, never required extra hard work.
weeklyTemplate.Sun: Low-fatigue upper body, supported hanging abs and a controlled hip direction before light evening ice; keep legs and wrist fresh for Monday.

phases.description: Establish repeatable baselines, wrist-tolerated movement, and a gradual return after holiday. All numeric doses are coaching prescriptions, not universal elite standards. Four gym slots are available, but symptom and game overrides take priority.

progressionProfile.skillDoseGate: Advance only after symptom-stable practice. Future larger doses are ceilings, not automatic increases.

If travel between them takes longer, perform the speed block separately or omit one accessory; never exceed the 60-minute gym budget or rush sprint recovery. Equipment choices replace their block; use only one choice.

warmup.note: Easy bike at RPE 2; on a track use a brisk walk/easy jog for the same time.
Eight ankle rocks per side.
Six slow hip switches in each direction.
Six comfortable lateral shifts per side.
Five reverse lunges with rotation per side.
Ten bridges, two-second top hold.
Three 10 m progressive accelerations at approximately 50%, 65% and 80%, one each minute including walking return. These are warm-up runs, not timed tests.

cooldown.note: Hold a comfortable position for 30 seconds each side. No bouncing or painful end range.
Six slow adductor rockbacks per side within this minute; do not force a hip pinch.

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift
cues: Stand centrally and brace before the pull.
Push the floor away and finish tall without leaning back.
mistakes: Jerking the bar from the floor.
Continuing when grip is painful or unreliable.
exercises.regression: Use higher handles with a lighter load; choose leg press if grip is not comfortable.
exercises.progression: Increase load using the lower-main rule while preserving the same handle height.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg, including the trap bar and all plates. Record handle height.

exercises.name: Wrist-comfortable safety-bar or back squat
cues: Choose a bar position that does not force the symptomatic wrist.
Keep the whole foot supported and descend to a controlled comfortable depth.
mistakes: Forcing the wrist into extension.
Adding depth or load while losing balance.
exercises.regression: Use a safety bar or leg press when a standard bar position is uncomfortable.
exercises.progression: Add load under the lower-main rule; retain the same depth for comparisons.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg, including the bar and all plates. Record bar type and squat depth.

exercises.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
cues: Keep most pressure through the front foot.
Let the front knee track with the toes and keep the pelvis level.
mistakes: Pushing hard from the rear leg.
Using a rear support so high it changes comfortable position.
exercises.regression: Use a floor split squat or light fingertip support.
exercises.progression: Add repetitions, then load; use a vest or other comfortable load if gripping is limited.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg across both hands or the vest. Bodyweight is not added to logged load.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
cues: Keep ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Finish with the hips extended and a brief glute squeeze.
mistakes: Finishing by arching the lower back.
Placing the bar directly on an unpadded hip crease.
exercises.regression: Use a floor glute bridge with bodyweight.
exercises.progression: Add load once every repetition reaches a controlled full finish.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg including bar and plates, or the displayed machine load. Record the variant and do not compare variants directly.

exercises.name: Leg press
cues: Keep the pelvis supported throughout.
Lower until the chosen range remains comfortable and controlled.
mistakes: Allowing the pelvis to roll from the pad.
Bouncing from the bottom or locking knees forcefully.
exercises.regression: Reduce load and range.
exercises.progression: Increase load under the lower-main rule; record machine and seat setting.
exercises.loadConvention: Total externally added machine kg or the displayed stack setting. Exclude unknown sled mass and record the exact machine and seat setting.

exercises.name: Seated hamstring curl
cues: Align the knee with the machine pivot.
Curl smoothly and control the return.
mistakes: Lifting the hips to move the weight.
Dropping the eccentric portion.
exercises.regression: Use a lighter load through a comfortable range.
exercises.progression: Add repetitions before the smallest available load increment.
exercises.loadConvention: Displayed machine kg. Record the same machine, settings and bilateral or unilateral version.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
cues: Soften the standing knee and hinge from the hip.
Keep both hip bones facing the floor.
mistakes: Opening the pelvis excessively.
Reaching farther by rounding the back.
exercises.regression: Use bodyweight and light support or a kickstand stance.
exercises.progression: Remove support before increasing comfortable load.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg held across all implements. Record the same hand and support arrangement.

exercises.name: Lateral lunge
exercises.quality: Lateral strength and controlled hip range
cues: Step wide enough to sit into the working hip.
Keep the working foot planted and push back under control.
mistakes: Forcing a groin stretch.
Letting the working knee collapse inward.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter step and shallow bodyweight range.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled range, then add load if the wrist permits.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg across all held implements. Bodyweight is not added to logged load.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip dumbbell floor press
cues: Keep palms facing each other and wrists stacked.
Touch the upper arms to the floor gently before pressing.
mistakes: Bending the wrist backward.
Bouncing the elbows or forcing painful range.
exercises.regression: Reduce load or use a comfortable neutral-handle press machine.
exercises.progression: Use upper-main progression only with comfortable gripping and stable wrists.
exercises.loadConvention: Kg per dumbbell. A pair of 20 kg dumbbells is logged as 20 kg; volume calculations must multiply external load by two.

exercises.name: Chest-supported neutral-grip row
cues: Keep the chest supported and wrists neutral.
Pull the elbows back without shrugging.
mistakes: Lifting the torso to finish a repetition.
Squeezing harder through wrist pain.
exercises.regression: Reduce load or use a supported machine with a comfortable handle.
exercises.progression: Add controlled repetitions, then load under upper-main progression.
exercises.loadConvention: For a two-dumbbell row, log the combined kg of both dumbbells. For a machine, log displayed stack kg and record the machine. Do not compare these variants directly.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip lat pulldown
cues: Keep a small stable torso lean.
Pull the elbows toward the ribs with neutral wrists.
mistakes: Swinging to move the stack.
Pulling behind the neck or through wrist pain.
exercises.regression: Reduce load and choose a comfortable handle width.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions or load with the same range and tempo.
exercises.loadConvention: Displayed cable-machine kg. Keep the machine, handle and settings identical for comparisons.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling landmine press
cues: Stack ribs over the pelvis.
Press up and forward without twisting.
mistakes: Arching the lower back.
Forcing the wrist around an uncomfortable bar end.
exercises.regression: Use a lighter bar or comfortable neutral-handle machine press.
exercises.progression: Add load once trunk position and wrist comfort remain consistent.
exercises.loadConvention: Total barbell and plate kg. This is a setup reference, not the force at the hand; record bar length and landmine arrangement.

exercises.name: Straight-knee calf raise
cues: Rise through the ball of the foot without rolling outward.
Pause briefly at the top and lower under control.
mistakes: Bouncing through repetitions.
Losing the foot tripod.
exercises.regression: Use two legs and support on a flat surface.
exercises.progression: Add range, then machine load or single-leg work.
exercises.loadConvention: Externally added machine kg or combined held kg. Do not include bodyweight; record unilateral or bilateral version.

exercises.name: Bent-knee calf raise
cues: Keep the knees bent and the forefoot supported.
Move the heels through a controlled comfortable range.
mistakes: Using hip movement to bounce the load.
Rushing the lowering phase.
exercises.regression: Perform seated bodyweight heel raises.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions, then machine load.
exercises.loadConvention: Externally added machine kg or displayed stack kg. Do not include bodyweight.

exercises.name: Short-lever Copenhagen hold
cues: Support the upper knee rather than the ankle initially.
Lift into a straight trunk line while breathing.
mistakes: Starting with a long lever before tolerating the short lever.
Continuing through groin pain.
exercises.regression: Use a side-lying adduction lift or shorter hold.
exercises.progression: Increase hold time or controlled repetitions before considering a longer lever.
exercises.loadConvention: Bodyweight hold. Log seconds and lever length; do not invent a kg load.

exercises.name: Band shoulder external rotation
cues: Keep the elbow close to the ribs with a small towel if useful.
Rotate the upper arm without twisting the torso.
mistakes: Pulling with the wrist.
Using a band too heavy to control.
exercises.regression: Use a lighter band and shorter comfortable range.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions before band resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Record band identity and tension setup in notes. A band colour is not a calibrated kg value.

exercises.name: Bodyweight split squat
cues: Use a stance that allows both knees to bend comfortably.
Lower straight down with pressure through the front foot.
mistakes: Walking a tightrope with the feet.
Letting balance failure dictate the range.
exercises.regression: Use light support and a shorter range.
exercises.progression: Increase comfortable range, then use a controlled loaded split squat.
exercises.loadConvention: Bodyweight repetitions. Log 0 external kg; do not add bodyweight to volume load.

exercises.name: Low step-up
cues: Place the whole working foot on the step.
Rise using the upper leg and lower slowly.
mistakes: Jumping from the trailing foot.
Using a step that causes pelvic twisting.
exercises.regression: Use a lower step and fingertip support.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled repetitions before height or load.
exercises.loadConvention: Bodyweight or total external kg across all implements. Record step height.

exercises.name: Hip abduction
cues: Keep the pelvis still.
Move through a comfortable range without leaning.
mistakes: Rotating the torso to move resistance.
Using momentum.
exercises.regression: Use side-lying bodyweight abduction.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions before machine or band resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Displayed machine kg, or band identity in notes. Do not assign an invented kg value to a band.

exercises.name: Assisted Nordic curl
cues: Keep hips extended as the body lowers.
Use enough assistance to control the movement.
mistakes: Falling onto a painful wrist.
Starting with unassisted full-range repetitions.
exercises.regression: Use seated hamstring curl or greater band assistance.
exercises.progression: Reduce assistance gradually while retaining control and a safe padded return.
exercises.loadConvention: Bodyweight with assistance. Record band or assistance setting in notes; do not report this as an estimated 1RM.

exercises.name: Belt squat, approved machine or attachment
equipment: Purpose-built belt-squat machine or approved attachment
exercises.quality: Lower-body force with reduced hand loading
cues: Use a load-rated belt and a purpose-built machine or manufacturer-approved attachment.
Keep the belt supported over the hips and squat with the whole foot planted.
Check the release and stop arrangement before the set.
mistakes: Treating an ordinary lifting belt as a loading attachment.
Improvising a hanging load or carrying a barbell squat weight into this setup.
exercises.regression: Use leg press or controlled bodyweight squats if an approved belt-squat setup is unavailable.
exercises.progression: Establish a fresh baseline for this exact setup, then use the prescribed strength progression without increasing pain or losing depth.
exercises.loadConvention: Total externally added kg on the approved belt-squat setup, or its verified kg display. Record the exact machine or attachment and starting position. Do not include bodyweight or unknown lever mass; establish a fresh baseline for every setup.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Confirm a load-rated squat belt on a purpose-built machine or manufacturer-approved attachment. An ordinary lifting belt alone is insufficient.

exercises.name: Cable hip flexion with ankle cuff
exercises.quality: Controlled forward leg drive and pelvic stability
cues: Fasten the cuff securely above the ankle and stand clear of the cable path.
Lift the working knee forward while keeping ribs stacked over a level pelvis.
Use light balance support only in a comfortable wrist position.
mistakes: Leaning backward to lift the leg.
Turning a controlled hip movement into a swinging kick.
exercises.regression: Use an unloaded standing march or reduce range and resistance.
exercises.progression: Reach the upper repetition target with a stable pelvis before the smallest available cable increment.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact cable station, pulley position and cuff setup. Log displayed kg only if the display is labelled kg; record other setting units in notes without inventing a kg conversion.

exercises.name: Cable hip extension with ankle cuff
cues: Face the cable with a secure ankle cuff and a slight standing-knee bend.
Move the working leg backward through a small comfortable range.
Keep the trunk and pelvis still instead of arching the lower back.
mistakes: Extending the back instead of the hip.
Using speed to pull the stack off its stops.
exercises.regression: Use an unloaded standing hip extension or floor glute bridge.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled repetitions before cable resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact cable station, pulley position and cuff setup. Log displayed kg only if the display is labelled kg; record other setting units in notes without inventing a kg conversion.

exercises.name: Cable hip abduction with ankle cuff
exercises.quality: Lateral hip strength and single-leg control
cues: Stand side-on and move the outer leg away from the cable.
Keep toes generally forward and the pelvis level.
Choose a range that does not require side-bending.
mistakes: Hiking the working hip.
Swinging the leg or leaning the torso to move a heavy stack.
exercises.regression: Use side-lying bodyweight abduction or a lighter cable setting.
exercises.progression: Complete the upper repetition target on both sides before increasing resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact cable station, pulley position and cuff setup. Log displayed kg only if the display is labelled kg; record other setting units in notes without inventing a kg conversion.

exercises.name: Cable hip adduction with ankle cuff
cues: Stand side-on with the cuff on the leg nearest the cable.
Bring the leg toward the midline through a comfortable range.
Keep the pelvis level and return slowly.
mistakes: Forcing a wide groin stretch.
Crossing farther by twisting the pelvis or swinging the leg.
exercises.regression: Use side-lying bodyweight adduction or less range and load.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions before the smallest cable increment; groin pain is a reason to reduce or omit.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact cable station, pulley position and cuff setup. Log displayed kg only if the display is labelled kg; record other setting units in notes without inventing a kg conversion.

exercises.name: Multi-hip machine: hip flexion
cues: Use this direction only if shown in the actual machine instructions.
Set the pivot and pad to the manufacturer positions before loading.
Lift the thigh forward with a level pelvis and controlled return.
mistakes: Assuming every multi-hip model permits hip flexion.
Setting the pad or pivot by copying another user.
exercises.regression: Use cable hip flexion or an unloaded standing march.
exercises.progression: Record the exact machine, pad settings and load; add controlled repetitions before resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Record machine, movement direction, pivot and pad settings. Log verified displayed kg only; keep a separate baseline for each machine and direction. A non-kg setting belongs in notes, not a fabricated kg value.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use only if the actual model explicitly supports this direction and its pad/pivot setup.

exercises.name: Multi-hip machine: hip extension
cues: Confirm the extension setup on the machine placard or manual.
Move the thigh backward while keeping ribs over the pelvis.
Use a controlled return without the stack dropping.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to extend farther.
Using an unsupported pad position or striking the stops.
exercises.regression: Use cable hip extension or a floor glute bridge.
exercises.progression: Reach the prescribed repetition range with the same machine settings before increasing resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Record machine, movement direction, pivot and pad settings. Log verified displayed kg only; keep a separate baseline for each machine and direction. A non-kg setting belongs in notes, not a fabricated kg value.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use only if the actual model explicitly supports this direction and its pad/pivot setup.

exercises.name: Multi-hip machine: hip abduction
cues: Set up the abduction direction exactly as shown for the model.
Move the thigh out to the side with the pelvis level.
Hold only the support needed for balance in a comfortable wrist position.
mistakes: Leaning or hiking the pelvis to move the pad.
Forcing range beyond the machine setup or personal tolerance.
exercises.regression: Use cable or side-lying hip abduction.
exercises.progression: Progress controlled repetitions before resistance with the same pivot and pad settings.
exercises.loadConvention: Record machine, movement direction, pivot and pad settings. Log verified displayed kg only; keep a separate baseline for each machine and direction. A non-kg setting belongs in notes, not a fabricated kg value.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use only if the actual model explicitly supports this direction and its pad/pivot setup.

exercises.name: Multi-hip machine: hip adduction
cues: Confirm the adduction setup for this model and start in a comfortable position.
Bring the thigh toward the midline without twisting the trunk.
Return slowly and stop before a painful groin stretch.
mistakes: Using an excessive starting range.
Letting the load pull the leg suddenly outward.
exercises.regression: Use light cable or side-lying hip adduction.
exercises.progression: Increase repetitions before resistance while retaining the same comfortable range.
exercises.loadConvention: Record machine, movement direction, pivot and pad settings. Log verified displayed kg only; keep a separate baseline for each machine and direction. A non-kg setting belongs in notes, not a fabricated kg value.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use only if the actual model explicitly supports this direction and its pad/pivot setup.

exercises.name: Pneumatic/hydraulic machine squat, model unconfirmed
equipment: Squat resistance machine, exact model to confirm
cues: Identify the model and follow its pad, stop and handgrip instructions before using this option.
Keep both feet grounded throughout the movement.
Maintain control of the carriage or exercise arm and lower smoothly.
mistakes: Assuming a power machine permits feet-off-platform jumping.
Releasing the exercise arm or treating a display setting as free-weight kilograms.
Increasing speed before the instructed use is confirmed.
exercises.regression: Use a familiar leg press or approved belt-squat setup with a fresh load reference.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled repetitions before the smallest verified setting change. Any fast-concentric use requires model-specific instruction; no jumping is prescribed.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact machine model, pad and stop positions, resistance setting and the units shown. No kg unit is assumed and loadKg remains blank. Machine settings are not converted to free-weight load, strength volume or estimated 1RM.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Model unconfirmed. The described equipment could be pneumatic (compressed air) rather than hydraulic. Follow the actual model instructions. Keep feet grounded; no machine jumps are prescribed.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Exhale gently and keep the ribs down.
Move only as far as the lower back position stays stable.
mistakes: Arching to reach farther.
Holding the breath throughout.
exercises.regression: Move one leg at a time with arms resting.
exercises.progression: Lengthen the leg lever or alternate opposite arm and leg.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Forearm side plank
cues: Place the elbow under the shoulder.
Keep hips aligned and breathe normally.
mistakes: Rotating the chest down.
Letting the hips sag.
exercises.regression: Bend the knees and shorten the hold.
exercises.progression: Extend the legs or increase the prescribed hold without losing position.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
cues: Roll the pelvis gently toward the ribs.
Lower slowly without swinging the legs.
mistakes: Throwing the legs overhead.
Using neck tension to finish.
exercises.regression: Use small posterior pelvic tilts.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled repetitions or slow the lowering phase.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Pallof press
cues: Stand or kneel square to the front.
Press away while resisting the sideways pull.
mistakes: Turning toward the cable.
Using painful grip to hold excessive resistance.
exercises.regression: Reduce resistance or use a forearm-supported alternative.
exercises.progression: Lengthen the pause before increasing comfortable resistance.
exercises.loadConvention: Displayed cable-machine kg, or band identity in notes. Keep the setup consistent.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
cues: Place elbows below shoulders and gently brace.
Maintain a straight trunk while breathing.
mistakes: Holding until the back sags.
Clenching the hands unnecessarily.
exercises.regression: Use knees on the floor or an elevated forearm support.
exercises.progression: Extend the lever or add a short hold within the target time.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Bird dog
cues: Reach long rather than high.
Keep the pelvis level and avoid shifting sideways.
mistakes: Arching the back.
Loading an uncomfortable extended wrist.
exercises.regression: Use a forearm-supported leg reach or a standing supported version.
exercises.progression: Add an opposite-arm reach and a controlled pause if wrist support is comfortable.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Ab-sling supported knee raise
exercises.quality: Controlled pelvic curl with reduced grip demand
cues: Use compatible load-rated slings and a secure anchor, with the upper arms supported as instructed.
Raise the knees and gently curl the pelvis toward the ribs.
Lower slowly and keep the body still between repetitions.
Stop if sling support causes shoulder pain or numbness.
mistakes: Swinging to lift the legs.
Assuming arm slings remove shoulder loading.
Adding weight before controlling bodyweight repetitions.
exercises.regression: Use a reverse crunch on the floor or a smaller knee-raise range.
exercises.progression: Add controlled repetitions, then gradually lengthen the leg lever while keeping the same pelvic curl.
exercises.loadConvention: Bodyweight knee raises. Log 0 external kg and the actual repetitions; bodyweight is not added to strength volume. Record sling setup and leg-lever variant.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Check rated slings, attachments and anchor. Slings reduce grip demand but still load the shoulders; stop with pain, tingling or numbness.

exercises.name: Standing broad jump
cues: Swing the arms and push the floor away.
Land quietly on two feet and hold the finish.
mistakes: Chasing distance with an uncontrolled landing.
Repeating while visibly fatigued.
exercises.regression: Use a submaximal jump or squat-to-calf-raise rehearsal.
exercises.progression: Increase jump intent while retaining a stable landing.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Lateral bound and stick
cues: Push sideways from one leg.
Land over the receiving foot and hold for two seconds.
mistakes: Letting the knee collapse inward.
Bounding farther than can be controlled.
exercises.regression: Use a lateral step and single-leg balance hold.
exercises.progression: Increase distance before adding continuous bounds.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Low pogo jumps
cues: Stay tall with low hops.
Use quick quiet contacts and stop if rhythm changes.
mistakes: Turning the drill into deep squat jumps.
Adding excessive contacts when sore.
exercises.regression: Use controlled calf raises or small marching bounces.
exercises.progression: Add a small number of contacts while maintaining short consistent contacts.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Single-leg forward hop and stick
cues: Take off and land on the same leg.
Hold the landing without a second hop.
mistakes: Using maximal distance before learning the landing.
Twisting through the knee.
exercises.regression: Use a small hop or forward step with a balance hold.
exercises.progression: Increase controlled distance gradually; log both sides separately.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Rotational medicine-ball scoop throw
cues: Turn through the hips and trunk together.
Use a light ball that can be accelerated crisply.
Release into an approved clear throw area, then collect the ball after it settles rather than catching a rebound.
mistakes: Twisting only through the lower back.
Throwing or catching through wrist pain.
exercises.regression: Use unloaded rotational footwork without a throw.
exercises.progression: Add intent or a step before a small ball-mass increase, only with comfortable wrists.
exercises.loadConvention: Actual medicine-ball mass in kg. Throw counts are separate from strength volume load.

exercises.name: Trap-bar jump
equipment: Collars and weight plates if needed
cues: Use a light total load that allows a crisp jump with comfortable, reliable gripping.
Stand centrally, brace, dip and jump vertically while keeping the bar level.
Land on two feet under control, settle fully, and reset before each repetition.
Stop when jump quality, grip or landing control changes.
mistakes: Using a heavy deadlift working weight for jumps.
Rebounding rapidly between repetitions or landing asymmetrically.
Treating a brace as permission to jump with painful gripping.
exercises.regression: Use an unloaded bilateral jump with a stable landing when gripping is unsuitable; omit jumping if lower-body symptoms or readiness limit it.
exercises.progression: Improve consistent take-off and landing quality first. Add only a small amount of load after reviewing actual jump quality; no automatic strength-style load increase.
exercises.loadConvention: Total external kg including the trap bar, plates and collars where known. Record handle height and actual jump repetitions. Each bilateral landing is two foot contacts; jump load is not used for Epley estimates or strength-volume progression.

exercises.name: Medicine-ball chest pass
equipment: Light medicine ball suitable for throwing
Approved wall or clear throw area
cues: Hold a light ball at chest height with comfortable wrists and ribs stacked.
Drive the ball forward quickly with a coordinated stance and clean release.
Allow the ball to settle before collecting it; catching a rebound is not prescribed.
Reset posture fully before the next throw.
mistakes: Choosing a ball so heavy that the throw becomes a slow press.
Catching a fast rebound with a symptomatic wrist.
Continuing after speed or control fades.
exercises.regression: Use unloaded coordinated arm and leg drive, or omit if the wrist is not comfortable.
exercises.progression: Increase crisp intent and consistency before a small ball-mass change; keep short sets and the prescribed recovery.
exercises.loadConvention: Actual medicine-ball mass in kg and actual throw repetitions. Optional distance is only logged when measured using a consistent setup. Throw counts are separate from strength volume and jump contacts.

exercises.name: 10 m acceleration
cues: Start still and push backward into the surface.
Rise gradually as speed builds.
mistakes: Rushing recovery between repetitions.
Sprinting on a slippery surface.
exercises.regression: Use a controlled 5 m acceleration or marching drill.
exercises.progression: Add quality repetitions before extending distance.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: 20 m acceleration
cues: Accelerate smoothly through the finish.
Leave clear space beyond the line to slow down.
mistakes: Braking before the finish.
Adding repetitions after technique deteriorates.
exercises.regression: Use 10 m accelerations.
exercises.progression: Increase speed consistency or a small number of repetitions with full recovery.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Sled push
cues: Use steady force through the legs with a stable trunk.
Choose a load that permits the intended quick steps.
mistakes: Making every repetition a slow grind.
Pushing through painful wrist support.
exercises.regression: Reduce load or use a belt-drag option if available and comfortable.
exercises.progression: Add distance or small load increments without losing the intended speed.
exercises.loadConvention: Added plate kg plus empty sled mass only when that mass is known. Record sled, surface and whether base mass is included.

exercises.name: 5-10-5 change of direction
cues: Lower the centre of mass before the turn.
Push away from each line with the knee tracking the foot.
mistakes: Comparing different line spacing.
Reaching for a line with a painful wrist.
exercises.regression: Practise controlled turns at reduced speed.
exercises.progression: Increase speed using identical distances and touch rules; train both start directions.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Chest-supported resisted runner, model unconfirmed
equipment: Chest-supported resisted running machine, exact model to confirm
cues: Identify the model and confirm the permitted exercise and setup with its instructions.
Adjust the chest support and secure the feet as the actual model requires.
Keep the torso supported and use the handles as instructed without painful gripping.
Alternate leg drive smoothly and bring the moving arms or pedals to a controlled stop.
mistakes: Treating the machine as a free-running treadmill or comparing its output with a track sprint.
Guessing what the resistance display units mean.
Training fast before learning the stops, supports and release procedure.
exercises.regression: Use a familiar indoor sled option if wrist-comfortable, or the prescribed easy-bike alternative when speed work is inappropriate.
exercises.progression: Record the exact model, support setting, resistance units and bout duration. Keep output crisp; any setting increase is specific to this machine, not a calculated sprint-speed gain.
exercises.loadConvention: Record the exact model, support settings, resistance setting and its actual units, bout seconds and optional displayed watts. No kg unit is assumed and loadKg remains blank. Do not record machine output as overground distance, sprint speed or a timed sprint result.
exercises.equipmentNotes: The chest-supported description resembles a resisted runner such as the Keiser A300, but the model is unconfirmed. This is a machine-specific alternative, not an overground sprint test.

exercises.name: Easy aerobic bike
exercises.quality: Aerobic base and easy recovery work
cues: Use a pace that allows complete sentences.
Keep breathing and cadence steady.
mistakes: Turning an easy session into a hard interval workout.
Leaning heavily through a painful wrist.
exercises.regression: Shorten the ride or use an easy walk.
exercises.progression: Increase easy duration before intensity.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Bike aerobic intervals
cues: Choose an effort repeatable across all work intervals.
Use the recovery period to bring breathing under control.
mistakes: Starting with a maximal sprint.
Ignoring a large output drop.
exercises.regression: Reduce work duration or use an easy continuous ride.
exercises.progression: Add one interval or extend work time under the phase prescription.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Bike short power intervals
exercises.quality: Brief high-power output with long recovery
cues: Accelerate decisively during the short work bout.
Take the complete prescribed easy recovery.
mistakes: Shortening recovery until speed collapses.
Using painful arm drive on the assault bike.
exercises.regression: Use a lower-intensity effort or legs-only stationary bike.
exercises.progression: Add a small number of high-quality repetitions before shortening recovery.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Bike repeated bursts
exercises.quality: Repeat hard efforts while managing fatigue
cues: Aim for consistent work output across rounds.
Use an honest session RPE after finishing.
mistakes: Adding this after an unexpectedly hard ice session.
Treating every repetition as an uncontrolled maximal effort.
exercises.regression: Reduce rounds or choose easy aerobic work.
exercises.progression: Progress only one of rounds, work time or recovery at a time.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Tempo run
cues: Run smoothly at the prescribed submaximal effort.
Maintain comfortable mechanics through each repetition.
mistakes: Turning tempo work into repeated sprinting.
Running fast on wet or icy ground.
exercises.regression: Use run-walk intervals or an easy bike.
exercises.progression: Add total controlled distance before increasing pace.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Easy walk
cues: Choose a comfortable conversational pace.
Use safe, well-lit footing.
mistakes: Treating the walk as a fitness test.
Forcing duration when unwell.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter indoor walk.
exercises.progression: Increase comfortable duration if desired.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Narrow stickhandling
cues: Keep the bottom hand relaxed enough to slide.
Use the same narrow lane when comparing scores.
mistakes: Counting uncontrolled taps as successful touches.
Continuing when wrist symptoms build.
exercises.regression: Slow down and shorten the bout.
exercises.progression: Increase clean contacts, then add a visual cue without increasing session duration.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Wide stickhandling
cues: Move the puck across the body within a comfortable reach.
Let the lower hand slide along the shaft.
mistakes: Reaching beyond the available pad.
Forcing wrist range at the end of the movement.
exercises.regression: Reduce width and speed.
exercises.progression: Add a small side-step while preserving control.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Forward-back stickhandling
cues: Move the puck forward and back beside the feet.
Keep the body quiet and the grip comfortable.
mistakes: Dragging with excessive force.
Losing the puck behind the body.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter forward-back path.
exercises.progression: Add a lateral movement to create a repeatable pattern.
exercises.loadConvention: No externally loaded strength target. Record the prescribed time, repetitions, distance or skill metric.

exercises.name: Figure-eight stickhandling
cues: Trace the same path around both markers.
Keep movements smooth before increasing speed.
mistakes: Changing marker spacing between tests.
Using wrist force to rescue every lost puck.
exercises.regression: Increase marker spacing and slow down.
exercises.progression: Reverse direction on an external cue.

testProtocols.name: Standing broad jump
protocol: Warm up for 5 minutes with easy cycling or jogging, then 8 squats, 5 reverse lunges per side and 2 submaximal practice jumps.
Place both toes behind a measured line, using the same foot width each time. Arm swing is allowed.
Jump forward from two feet and land on two feet. Hold the landing for 2 seconds without falling or stepping back.
Measure from the take-off line to the nearest heel. Record centimetres.
Complete 3 valid attempts with 90 seconds rest between attempts. Keep all values and use the best valid distance.
testProtocols.frequency: Baseline after familiarisation; programme test weeks 1, 10, 18, 26, 34, 42 and 50. Use recovered conditions.
precautions: Use the same surface, shoes, equipment and measurement method at each assessment.
Record sleep, soreness, recent training and any symptoms. Testing replaces a workout; it is not an extra maximal session.
Postpone a maximal test if unwell, injured or unable to perform the movement normally.
A fall, backwards step or one-foot landing invalidates that attempt.
Do not compare jump tests performed with different arm rules or measurement conventions.

testProtocols.name: 10 m acceleration
protocol: Use a dry, flat track with a clear run-off area. Mark 0 m and 10 m accurately.
After a dynamic warm-up, complete 3 progressive 20 m runs at approximately 60%, 75% and 90% effort, with 60 seconds rest.
Use a standing start with the front toe behind 0 m. Start from stillness without rocking or a run-up.

For fixed video timing, time from the first visible movement until the torso crosses 10 m. Record the frame rate and timing definition. With timing gates, record the exact start offset and gate configuration as a separate protocol.
Run 3 maximal trials, resting 3 minutes between trials. Keep the best valid time and the timing method.

testProtocols.name: Pro agility 5-10-5 yard course in metric units
protocol: Place three parallel lines with the outer lines 4.572 m to either side of the centre line. The full width is 9.144 m.
Practise the sequence at half speed once in each direction. Start straddling the centre line in the same documented stance each time.
Run 4.572 m to the first line and touch it with the hand, turn and run 9.144 m to the opposite line and touch it, then turn and run 4.572 m through the centre.
For video timing, start at first movement and stop as the torso crosses the centre line on the final return.
Complete 2 valid trials starting left and 2 starting right, resting 3 minutes between trials. Record the best time in each direction.

testProtocols.name: Original 40 m 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test
protocol: Use the original 40 m official 30-15 IFT audio. Mark lines at 0 m, 20 m and 40 m with the official 3 m tolerance zones and space beyond each end.
Complete a light dynamic warm-up and practise following the audio before the assessment.
Run for 30 seconds and recover for 15 seconds. The original first stage is 8 km/h, increasing by 0.5 km/h every stage.
During each 15-second recovery, walk forward to the next marked line as directed by the audio. Do not walk backwards to a closer line.
Stop at voluntary exhaustion or when unable to reach the end-zone tolerance on three consecutive occasions.
Record the speed of the last fully completed stage as VIFT. Complete only one maximal test that day.

testProtocols.name: Submaximal strength reference
protocol: Choose the usual wrist-tolerated main lift. Record its exact variant, equipment, depth or handle height and any straps.
Complete the session warm-up, then 3 gradual practice sets of 5, 3 and 2 repetitions at easy effort, resting 60, 90 and 120 seconds respectively.
Perform one technically consistent reference set of 3 to 6 repetitions at RPE 7 to 8, leaving approximately 2 to 3 repetitions in reserve. Rest 3 minutes before the set.
Record load, completed repetitions, RPE, technique and symptoms. Stop if form changes or pain appears.
For tracking only, calculate Epley estimate = load in kg x (1 + repetitions / 30). Save the actual set as the primary observation.

testProtocols.name: Controlled stickhandling quality reference
protocol: Use the same stick, Green Biscuit or ball, floor surface and two markers 30 cm apart each time.

After 60 seconds rest, repeat once. Keep both trials and compare controlled touches together with error count, wrist response and eyes-up percentage.

testProtocols.name: Shooting target accuracy reference
protocol: Use the same safe shooting setup, puck, pad, stick, shot type and measured distance. Default reference distance is 3 m where safe space permits.
Set five fixed target areas: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right and five-hole. Record each target size and position before the first test.
After 5 comfortable non-counted practice shots and 60 seconds rest, take 5 shots at each target, for 25 counted attempts total.
Rest 15 seconds between shots and 60 seconds between target groups. Use one shot type for each test.
Record attempts and hits by zone. Accuracy = total hits / total attempts x 100. Keep speed and release time separate if measured.

testProtocols.name: Single-leg lateral hop and stick
protocol: Mark the centre of the starting heel on a dry, stable surface. Keep hands on hips.
Stand on the right leg, hop laterally to the right, and land on the right leg. For the left leg, mirror the task to the left.
Hold each landing for 2 seconds with the free foot off the floor and without hopping again.
Measure lateral displacement from the starting heel centre to the landing heel centre.
Complete 3 valid trials per side, alternating legs, resting 60 seconds between attempts. Record the best distance for each side.
